name: Greece
eligibility: One law firm's account states that judicial permission is required before embryo transfer to another woman, that a medical indication is required, that the carrying woman may not provide the ova, and that residency in Greece is required of the applicant or the carrier. This is a commercial source and is recorded as such, not as a verified statutory position.
paymentModel: The same source states that payment for services and any kind of financial benefit is strictly prohibited.
parentage: Not verified. No statutory text was retrievable for this page.

facts.claim: Gestation by another woman requires prior judicial permission and a medical indication, the carrying woman may not provide the ova, and financial benefit to her is prohibited.

source.label: Surrogacy proceedings in Greece (law firm page)
source.supports: A law firm's practice page. It is internally inconsistent: it cites Law 3089/2002, where the assisted reproduction statute is normally given as Law 3087/2002. Recorded because it is the only openable account found, and flagged because the statute number it names is wrong.

openQuestions: The Greek statute itself was not read for this page. Until the numbered law and its amendments are confirmed, nothing on this page should be relied on.
